steps.what: Check the immediate crisis context and available service contacts
Clarify the patient's immediate needs and wishes
Choose an appropriate crisis advocacy response
Write the necessary advocacy request and relevant supporting facts
Advocate with the outside service and deliver the checked request
Write the crisis outcome and next action in the patient record

tasks.design: Use a native crisis-context view in the {OTHER} patient case system, current service contacts in {DOCS}, and reusable request and outcome headings. The social worker chooses and carries out the advocacy, writes the actual request separately from the call and keeps the outcome in the patient record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service contacts and relevant patient facts are repeatedly searched and copied during a crisis.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case views and request templates may reduce those clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency, patient wishes and a provider's limited capacity need active judgement and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The social worker can press for an appropriate response while recognizing changing risk.
tasks.altitude: A little less clerical handling leaves more attention for advocacy; crisis authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Help a patient contact appropriate support
reach.learn: Crisis escalation routes and clear factual handoffs

evidence.claim: Native context views and request templates can remove repeated field copying while leaving crisis judgement human; savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes the patient discussion, real advocacy-request writing, outside-service handoff and the outcome record used for ongoing care. Immediate emergencies do not wait for a form.

OTHER means the patient case system. The care team supplies existing identity and clinical facts; the social worker establishes immediate need in s2, writes requested action and necessary facts in s4, and records the service response in s6. Retained12 retrieval,9 request and8 outcome hours count capture and verification. Missing facts use direct manual checking.
Test native views and headings before code. No service-availability flag, risk score or automated crisis send is assumed.
The request's ordinary author save has no gate or save-time saving. Its external communication is separately gated on the exact request; the outcome write is not self-approved.
unknowns: Frequency of written requests versus wholly verbal advocacy
research_questions: How much clerical time can be removed without delaying urgent advocacy or weakening source checks?

steps.what: Review current clinical guidance and the patient's documented situation
Choose appropriate end-of-life information within professional scope
Prepare the relevant approved information sheet
Provide the checked information sheet to the patient
Educate clients about symptoms and options and check their understanding
Write what was explained and the patient's questions in the care record

tasks.design: Use a current guidance index and approved information layouts in {DOCS}, with the existing education fields in the {OTHER} patient case system. The social worker chooses suitable information, explains it with the patient and writes the actual education record separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current information is searched again and repeated education headings are re-entered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document indexes and education forms may reduce search, layout and repeated headings.
tasks.still_hard: Readiness, uncertainty and deeply personal choices cannot be resolved by a handout.
tasks.human_edge: The social worker notices distress and adapts the pace and language without directing the patient's choice.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation saving can protect time for questions; no clinical decision authority changes.

evidence.claim: Approved document indexes and native education headings can reduce repeated preparation and entry; this is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes information preparation, handout delivery, the conversation and its real care-record entry. It does not automate end-of-life advice or a patient's decision.

The clinical guidance owner supplies dated approved content; the care team supplies existing clinical context. The social worker selects relevant sections in s1-s3 and produces topic, information provided, questions and understanding in s5-s6. Retained12 source,7.5 preparation and12 record hours count checking and capture. Missing clinical context is checked manually with the care team.
OTHER means the patient case system. Test native indexes and education forms before code. No generated prognosis, inferred preference or automated patient send is introduced.
An ordinary author save of the education record has no gate and no saving. This education record is distinct from assessment and care-plan entries in258 and265.
unknowns: Approved accessible information formats and existing education fields
research_questions: Can native guidance links shorten preparation while preserving appropriate clinical scope and patient comprehension?

already_counted.description: Information checks, content choice, patient discussion, handover and education record

incremental.description: Flag stale information links and correct education headings

The specific explanations and options discussed with this patient, checked within scope as spoken

steps.what: Gather relevant consultation findings and patient context
Collaborate with other professionals to evaluate the patient's condition
Assess the client's social needs in light of the findings
Write the assessment findings and unresolved questions in the patient record

tasks.design: Use native consultation links and assessment headings in the {OTHER} patient case system. Keep the multidisciplinary exchange and social assessment human, and separate the actual written assessment from the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consultation sources and repeated assessment headings are spread across screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and structured headings can reduce navigation and repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Different professionals may disagree or be describing different time periods.
tasks.human_edge: The social worker tests relevance, uncertainty and the social implications of clinical findings.
tasks.altitude: Less copying can leave more time to resolve conflicting evidence.

reach.task: Contribute social-context findings to multidisciplinary assessment

evidence.claim: Native source links and assessment forms can reduce retrieval and repeated headings; local benefits are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes evidence gathering, internal care-team collaboration, assessment judgement and its real written record. Patient care-plan writing is separately counted in265.

Consulting professionals produce dated findings. The social worker checks patient identifier, author, date, finding, uncertainty and source in s1 and produces the social assessment in s3-s4. Retained17 retrieval and15 writing hours include checking and capture; missing findings are clarified manually.
OTHER means the patient case system. Test native links and forms before code; no free structured needs code or risk field is assumed.

This baseline is collaboration with colleagues inside the organisation, so authority is internal. No additional outside-provider send is automated or claimed. The author's assessment save has no self-approval gate and no saving.
unknowns: Native consultation links and current assessment format
research_questions: Do native links remove navigation while keeping conflicting findings visible?

already_counted.description: Evidence checks, collaboration, social judgement and substantive assessment writing

incremental.description: Correct assessment headings and source links

High: compatible native links save two retrieval hours and reused assessment headings save three writing hours, R95 plus1 upkeep, net4; collaboration and judgement retain60 hours.

tasks.short: Plan, coordinate and follow through on care

steps.what: Review consultation data and the current patient care position
Choose appropriate care and rehabilitation arrangements with the patient
Write the care plan and the required service request
Coordinate with the outside provider and communicate the final service request
Follow through with the patient and provider to check service efficacy
Update the care plan with the actual follow-up outcome

tasks.design: Use a native care-context view in {OTHER} and reusable care-plan fields to reduce repeated source navigation and entry. The social worker chooses the arrangements, writes the plan and request, communicates with the provider, checks actual efficacy and updates the plan in its later phase.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consultation facts and stable patient details are copied into plans and follow-up entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plan forms and source links can remove repeated fields without choosing care or inferring success.
tasks.still_hard: A completed referral does not show that the service is accessible or effective.
tasks.human_edge: The social worker checks what actually changed for the patient and renegotiates arrangements when needed.
tasks.altitude: A small clerical saving protects follow-through; care decisions stay with the relevant professionals and patient.

evidence.claim: Native care-plan forms and source links can reduce repeated fields while coordination and efficacy judgement remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes consultation review, care choice, real plan and request writing, provider coordination, later efficacy checking and the actual plan update. Assessment authorship in258 is reused once.

OTHER means the patient case system. The care team produces consultation data; the social worker checks patient identifier, source date and current need in s1 and writes goals, service, responsible party and review date in s3. Retained12 retrieval and14 plan-writing hours count capture and checking. Missing data require manual verification.

The patient and provider produce the actual response in s5; the social worker captures outcome, uncertainty and next action in s6, whose8 retained hours include that work. No completion flag, efficacy score or outcome metadata appears for free.
Test native views and forms before code. No automated request send, reminder or plan commit is proposed. Same-system author saves have no gate and no saving.
unknowns: Current plan form and service-request format
Whether stable fields can be reused across native records
research_questions: Does field reuse remove copying while preserving individual goals and real follow-up outcomes?

already_counted.description: Context checks, care choice, substantive plan writing, provider coordination and efficacy follow-through

approvals.approved_version: The specific care options and arrangements discussed with this patient; changes require renewed checking

The specific follow-up questions and information shared with this patient and provider, checked as spoken

High: a compatible native plan removes four initial-writing hours, two retrieval hours and one update-heading hour, R93 plus1 upkeep, net6; care choice and all35 coordination and follow-through hours stay full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated record navigation and fields while protecting advocacy, sensitive education and care follow-through.
role.ambitious_version: A healthcare social worker who keeps useful care records and has more attention for patients and provider follow-through.
